patterns_data.top_pattern: Auth status and facility mapping shifts must be validated before action
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / authorization and facility mapping in CA, NV, OH, VA, and KY
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the apparent cost change is tied to shifts in authorization coding and unmapped facility values rather than confirmed changes in utilization or reimbursement. Because these shifts sit in front of operational action, they should be cleared first so UM, policy, and provider teams do not act on distorted signals.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If the auth or facility classification moved, downstream rate, utilization, and provider decisions could target the wrong problem.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a focused validation on AUTH_CODE_DISTRIBUTION and Not Mapped facility records in CA, NV, OH, VA, and KY, reconcile them to claim-level authorization status and facility type, and only then route confirmed changes to UM or reimbursement policy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Large dollar movement is explicitly tied to auth distribution changes and unmapped facility values, so the signal must be validated before business action.
evidence_summary: NV auth code distribution changes tied to Lucile Packard added +$7.7M.
CA auth code distribution changes tied to Hoag added +$3.5M.
OH auth code distribution changes tied to Ohio State added +$2.1M.
CA and KY claims recorded as Not Mapped facility type added about +$329K.

patterns_data.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is concentrated in a few commercial provider and auth segments
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / CA / ACUTE HOSPITAL / PPO and HMO
key_driver_codes: Cesarean Section without Sterilization without CC/MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: CA acute hospital pressure is concentrated in a small number of commercial segments, especially PPO and HMO business tied to Hoag and a small set of high-cost DRGs. The increase is not purely utilization-driven: PA-required admissions are rising in some slices, while non-PA maternity and back-problem claims still show residual price pressure even when volume is flat or down.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: This is large enough to need a combined UM, contracting, and provider-management response rather than a single-point review.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open a CA acute hospital workplan that separates PA-required from non-PA claims, starts with Hoag and other concentrated providers, and pairs admission management with DRG-level reimbursement review for ungroupable, maternity, and back-problem cases.
evidence_summary: CA PPO acute hospital findings added +$13.9M, including +$4.4M at Hoag on 51 more PA-required admissions.
PA-required ungroupable PPO acute cases in CA added +$5.5M on 18 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $81K.
CA HMO acute claims added +$832K, mostly at Hoag with 17 more admissions and paid per admit up about $27K.
Non-PA CA PPO maternity added +$755K even with 100 fewer admissions, showing residual unit-cost pressure.

patterns_data.pattern_details: This inpatient story is concentrated in a small number of very high-cost specialty and ungroupable admissions rather than broad Med/Surg drift. The individual cases carry unusually high paid per admit and several occur off very low baselines, so the right response is case-level clinical and payment review, not broad utilization tightening.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few catastrophic or misclassified admissions can create outsized cost swings and warrant immediate case-level action.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Prioritize case-by-case clinical and payment validation for the identified high-cost stays, starting with Lucile Packard, Hoag, NYU, and Ohio State specialty admissions, and confirm severity, grouping, and payment accuracy before broader policy changes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in small numbers of rare, specialized, and sometimes ungroupable admissions with low-baseline flags.
evidence_summary: Lucile Packard allogeneic bone marrow transplant cases added +$6.5M on 1 more admission.
CA rare ungroupable IP Med/Surg cases such as spinal cord injury and cirrhosis each added about +$1.6M to +$2.7M on 1 to 2 admissions.
NYU cardiac valve procedures added +$1.3M on 3 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $322K.
Many of these inpatient spikes are low-volume or ungroupable, so case-level validation is required.

patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IP OB Dlvry/Well NB, IP NICU, and maternity-related Acute Hospital claims across Commercial Local Group
key_driver_codes: Cesarean Section without Sterilization with CC
Cesarean Section without Sterilization without CC/MCC
MAT CARE LW TRANS SCAR PREV C/S DEL
ABN FETL HEART RATE RHYTHM COMP L&D
GESTATIONAL HTN W/O SIGN PU COMP CB
Extreme Immaturity or Respiratory Distress Syndrome, Neonate
patterns_data.pattern_details: Maternity cost growth is recurring across several states and products, with C-section episodes showing both higher volume and pockets of higher acuity. The clinical drivers point to repeat C-section history, fetal distress, post-term pregnancy, hypertensive complications, and some neonatal escalation, so this is a care-pathway issue more than a single provider anomaly.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Maternity is recurring enough to support focused clinical, UM, and reimbursement action rather than one-off case review.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route this to maternity clinical and UM teams to review repeat C-section patterns, delivery management, neonatal escalation, and state-level reimbursement differences for the highest-growth C-section pathways.
evidence_summary: Multistate PPO acute maternity findings added +$7.0M, led by C-section DRGs in NY and OH.
CA maternity clinical findings added +$3.3M, led by prior C-section scar, fetal heart rhythm issues, post-term pregnancy, and pre-eclampsia.
CT PPO acute C-section claims added +$3.7M, including +$1.3M for C-section with CC and +$530K without CC/MCC.
VA neonatal and OB findings added about +$624K, including NICU respiratory distress and repeat C-section-related cases.

patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Review referral pathways, case eligibility, and contractual terms for Lucile Packard children's episodes across CA, NV, NY, and OH, and separate unavoidable tertiary care from steerable utilization.

patterns_data.top_pattern: Post-acute facility use is adding cost through LTCH and rehab settings
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Commercial Local Group / LONG TERM CARE HOSPITAL and Physical Rehab in CA, GA, IN, and VA
patterns_data.pattern_details: Cost is shifting into LTCH and rehab settings, especially for aftercare and ungroupable stays, with both more admissions and very high per-admit payment. This points to a post-acute level-of-care and site-of-care issue following the initial hospital stay.

key_driver_codes: Cesarean Section without Sterilization without CC/MCC
patterns_data.pattern_details: Several small state-product slices are showing localized emergence off low baselines, often in maternity-related acute settings and occasionally in critical access facilities. These are real enough to audit, but too small and uneven to justify enterprise-wide rule changes unless they persist.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Small-volume pockets can signal a developing issue, but acting too broadly too early would overcorrect for limited local variation.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Assign these states to local UM and provider operations for targeted case review and repeatability checks, with emphasis on low-volume price spikes and critical access maternity-related claims.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Most of these pockets carry low-baseline or small-volume characteristics, so confirm repeatability before expanding policy action.
evidence_summary: WI POS acute claims added +$268K on 22 more admissions.
NH HMO critical access claims added +$195K on 12 more admissions, with paid per admit up about $16K.
VA POS acute unit-cost pressure added +$197K despite 30 fewer admissions.
NH POS acute unit-cost pressure added +$139K with no volume change, confirming a low-volume price issue.
